messages:
kat: Hey — running into TLS errors when pointing the Python SDK at our Private base_url behind the corporate proxy. Works with hosted API, but Dedicated VPC + custom CA fails with `certificate verify failed`

kat: Minimal repro: I initialize the client with base_url and try streaming and the request fails on verify.

kat: Code:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key='x', base_url='https://private.redwood.local', ca_bundle='/etc/ssl/redwood_ca.pem')
resp = client.generate('hello')
print(resp)
```

kat: Error: `requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed` even though `/etc/ssl/redwood_ca.pem` contains the organization's CA.

ajay: hmm — are you using the sync or async client? httpx vs requests behavior differs.

kat: sync for that snippet. I also tried AsyncClient and same cert path passed via `verify=` in the client ctor but still fails when base_url is set to the private host. If I hit the public hosted API with the same cert path it works (weird).

tom: @kat can you paste `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect private.redwood.local:443` output (redact certs) — maybe the server chains differently in the VPC so requests' CA bundle lookup doesn't match?

kat: quick output: server sends leaf + intermediate; chain looks fine. I can curl with `--cacert /etc/ssl/redwood_ca.pem` and it succeeds. So cert and chain are OK.

maria: this sounds like a client-level proxy/path resolution issue. Are you setting `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` env vars? httpx/request session behavior can ignore `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` depending on how the SDK constructs sessions.

kat: I tried `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/redwood_ca.pem` and also `export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/redwood_ca.pem` — still fails when base_url points to the private host. If I remove base_url and proxy, hosted works.

ajay: Possible bug: when base_url is set we replace underlying session and forget to pass `verify` or to load env var into the session. Also we have custom proxy wiring for Dedicated that might be switching to urllib3's PoolManager without passing CA.

tom: Also worth noting: the async client's typing for `stream()` is incomplete so people do weird workarounds and instantiate their own httpx client which leads to differing verify/proxy. Filing two separate issues: TLS verify w/ base_url+ca_bundle+proxy, and missing type hints for async streaming.

kat: Filed a short repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood-samples/private-ca-repro (link placeholder) — includes sync + async minimal examples and curl that succeeds.

maria: Workaround for now: call `requests.Session()` yourself and mount an adapter with your `certifi.where()` patched? Ugly but it gets around the SDK's session creation. Example:
```python
import requests
s = requests.Session()
s.verify = '/etc/ssl/redwood_ca.pem'
# use s to perform handshake to the host, then pass tokens to SDK calls
```

ajay: I'm going to dig into the SDK code. I suspect we call `requests.Session()` correctly for sync, but when base_url is present we create a custom `HTTPAdapter`/PoolManager and forget to set `cert_reqs`/`ca_certs`. For async, httpx expects `verify` param path or `trust_env=True/False`.

dev-bot: CI run for PR #4031 completed — all tests passed :white_check_mark:

tom: For the typing request: the async client lacks `-> AsyncIterator[StreamChunk]` annotations for `.stream()` which makes mypy noisy. If you can include a short note in the issue we can prioritize it.

kat: Thanks. Please include the proxy angle — corporate proxy seems to change the failure footprint. Also we saw a flaky fallback where the SDK silently retries with no verify flag (not ideal).

maria: Action items: ajay will open a single GH issue that: 1) reproduces TLS failure with base_url + custom CA + proxy, 2) notes async vs sync behavior, 3) includes typing missing for stream. I'll tag the runtime and sdk teams.

ajay: I'll open the issue and link the gist. Will cc @eng-runtime and @devex. ETA tomorrow morning.

kat: Appreciated — happy to pair on repro.

maria: marking as p0 for DX since this blocks Private onboarding. :exclamation:
